caveats: 2020 contributes 71.1% of net Development trade-return improvement for the growth nominee and 90.1% for the drawdown nominee; removal of 2020 leaves net improvement positive and the benefit appears in 13/17 and 14/17 years respectively.
Growth Holdout wealth improved but max drawdown and daily CVaR were slightly worse than baseline; the candidate survives as a growth policy, not as a drawdown-control policy.
The diagnostic risk-budget convention permits borrowing and reached extreme gross exposure; it is not a deployment recommendation and was not used for nomination.

Stages 3-4 used an open-aware transaction simulator whose internal baseline differs from the Stage 1-2 baseline by about 0.05%; all Stage 3-4 conclusions are relative to their own matched baseline and no policy advanced.
The prior dynamic-stop null study has separate known protocol-compliance caveats and is motivational only; the present candidate does not depend on that null for validity.

stage1.finding: Simple ATR/realized-vol sizing improved portfolio path but failed frozen breadth/cluster gate.

stage2.finding: Genome/family causal expected-return divided by p10-loss sizing produced the only independently robust Development candidates.

stage3.finding: No graduated-entry policy cleared baseline wealth/risk usefulness.

stage4.finding: No partial de-risk policy cleared baseline wealth/risk usefulness.

stage5.reason: Stage 1 failed breadth; Stages 3 and 4 failed independent wealth/risk usefulness. Protocol forbids unrestricted combinations of failed components.
